fieldMarks: Male: black with a yellow head and white wing patches that stand out in flight
Female: smaller, sooty brown with yellow on the face and chest, white streaks on the belly and no white wing patches
Immatures have some yellow on the head and small or absent wing patches
behavior: Migrates in flocks; males may winter farther north than females
Forages mostly walking in open fields or at water edges; may follow farm machinery; usually in flocks with other blackbirds outside nesting
Feeds heavily on insects in summer; about two-thirds of diet is seeds
Harsh, incessant oka-wee-wee and kruck calls that blend into a wavering chorus in colonies
habitat: Breeds in freshwater sloughs, marshy lake borders and tall cattails in water up to 3-4 ft deep; forages around marshes and in pastures, plowed fields and feedlots.
range: Breeds from central-interior British Columbia east to extreme western Ontario and northwestern Ohio, south to southern California, New Mexico and northern Texas; winters from central California, Arizona and Texas south into Mexico.
